text:
This looks like early-to-mid 2017. The fed funds rate is about 0.91%, which fits March–April 2017 (the rate was around 0.9% after the March hike). The 10-year yield is 2.42% and headline CPI is 2.8% YoY, which matches February 2017 (CPI 2.7%) or perhaps March. The unemployment rate of 4.7% matches January or February 2017.

The fed funds effective rate was 0.66% in January and 0.66% in February 2017, then 0.79% in March and 0.91% in April–May. The December 2016 effective rate was 0.54%, rising to 0.65% in January. The 3-month change of +0.36 and 12-month change of +0.66 fit a rate of 0.91 against 0.25 a year earlier, which would be about 0.36 in early 2016. That points to March–April 2017.

The 2-year yield was 1.28% at the end of March 2017 and 10-year 2.40%. At the end of April the 2-year was about 1.28% and the 10-year 2.28%. March 2017 fits the 10-year best at 2.42%. Unemployment was 4.7% in March 2017 (it fell to 4.5% in April). CPI YoY in March 2017 was 2.4%, and in February 2.7%, so 2.8% doesn't fit exactly. Equity returns of -0.6% for the month don't fit March 2017, when the S&P was about flat at +0.1%. Gold +1.0% and EM +3.9% fit March.

Fed funds at 0.91 may be a December 2016 reading plus a later hike, but the 10-year at 2.42% could fit Dec 2016 (2.45%). In December 2016, though, CPI was 2.1%, and the Fed funds effective rate was 0.54%. March 2017 therefore stays the best fit.
